csv_project_name: AE for SECOG Eastern Shoreline Path Facilities
csv_scope_of_work: The Southeastern Connecticut Council of Governments (SECOG) is seeking the services of a transportation engineer or transportation planning and engineering firm to provide planning-level design for Eastern Shoreline Path facilities within Waterford, Connecticut.The selected firm/individual will assist the SECOG staff with planning and preliminary engineering and estimation of Waterford sections of the Eastern Shoreline Path. Duties may include but are not limited to the following: Gather and evaluate relevant data including, but not limited to, traffic volume, crashes, signals, speed data, rights-of-way (regional database), topography, environmental resource data, utility, structural data, land use data, crash data, and review of current geometry and planned and programmed road projects. Develop and evaluate facility alternatives (e.g. shared use path, separated bike lanes, bike lanes, sharrows) for feasibility and appropriateness. Create an Eastern Shoreline Path Bikeway wayfinding signage plan showing locations of all directional signs. Create planning level (30%) design of the recommended facility, including interim and long-term solutions. Evaluate impacts to rights-of-way. Enumerate permitting coordination requirements, and utility relocations. Gather pavement, bridge, and drainage data as available. Estimate costs, including phase breakout if appropriate. Stakeholder and public engagement, including at least one (1) in person opportunity for public input and utilization of digital engagement.
csv_disciplines_requested: Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Planning/Master Planning, Traffic Design Engineering, Transportation Planning, Graphic Design/Public Art

relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a transportation planning and preliminary engineering assignment, not structural design.
- Focus is on bikeway/path corridor alternatives, signage, right-of-way, and public engagement.
- Any bridge component is only incidental through collection of available bridge data; no bridge design is defined.
- Includes planning disciplines rather than a clear structural or special-structure scope.
